Read-only soundness review for Bifrost issue #7314 (parent session 28c4a33b). Your brief is /workspace/28c4a33bde5b6bc0b4f4d45aa56e46bd/bifrost-dev/.mj/lanes/logs/c1-4e/COMPLETE-RISK-BRIEF.md; read it first. In short: two native C# definition answers on jellyfin claimed complete (correct target) where legacy was incomplete. Determine whether native's simple-name member lookup is sound when the enclosing type has a base list with external entries, overloads, partial parts or extension methods. Use the two real rows and small fixtures.
Rules:
- No commits or tree changes.
- Scratch work under /tmp only.
- No cloud calls.
- Prefix cargo with `env -u RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN -u CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`, and build with --profile measure --features test-support at master 947d10e0f1, in a /tmp worktree.
Write REPORT.md to .mj/lanes/logs/c1-4e/complete-risk/ and hand back the items at the end of the brief.
I’ll read the review brief, trace the two jellyfin rows through the native resolver, and test the suspected cases in the requested temporary worktree.
The C# route marks an inherited-type gap when an owner-member lookup misses. I’m checking whether the same gap reaches completion when a local member is found, which is the case in both rows.

The source confirms that BaseItem’s listed bases are interfaces and that BaseItemMapper is a static class. Both local calls therefore have a plausible complete target; the remaining risk is whether a partial declaration can contribute a competing overload that the native read misses.

The requested measure profile build is still compiling `bifrost-store` on the shared host. The fixture probe is queued behind that build; I’ll use its output to separate proven behavior from source based inference in the report.
The build has passed the store and analysis crates and is compiling the test harness. I have not changed the project tree; the probe exists only in the disposable `/tmp` worktree.

The shared host is slow enough that the targeted build is taking several minutes, but it is still making progress. The source review already isolates the likely fix point: completion coverage at the C# owner lookup, especially when several partial parts contribute members.
The test build has reached the root dependencies. Once it completes, I’ll run one additional partial overload probe if the first fixture does not exercise competing applicable signatures.
The build remains active under heavy concurrent Rust compilation. I’m recording the source findings now so the review result is durable, then I’ll add the fixture outputs if the harness finishes.

The first fixture pass returned incomplete for all four compact one-line cases because the binding itself carried an incomplete diagnostic. I rewrote those fixtures as ordinary multiline C# to remove that parser shape as a confounder and am rerunning the same targeted probe.

Review delivered to the parent. Both jellyfin answers are sound; four small fixtures returned incomplete answers. The [report](/workspace/28c4a33bde5b6bc0b4f4d45aa56e46bd/bifrost-dev/.mj/lanes/logs/c1-4e/complete-risk/REPORT.md) records the remaining partial-overload risk and test evidence.

Parent (28c4a33b): thanks; the two rows are settled. Your finding that "positive paths can bypass the inherited guard" needs one decisive follow-up, because the tiny fixtures were incomplete everywhere and masked it. Build fixtures with PROVEN membership: a plain SDK-style csproj under Microsoft.NET.Sdk, no Directory.Build files, all sources under the project directory. Confirm a simple local declaration answers complete first, as the control. Then, under BIFROST_TRIAL_NATIVE_CSHARP, test:
(a) `class B { public void M() {} } class D : B { void M(int x) {} void Caller() { M(); } }`. C# overload resolution picks B.M, because D.M(int) is not applicable to M(). Does native answer D.M as complete?
(b) The same, with B external (an unresolvable base) and D.M(int) local.
(c) A non-partial class with two same-name local overloads and a call that only one fits. Is it complete-ambiguous, or complete on one?
(d) A partial class whose parts in two files declare competing overloads.
Report each answer and its completion. If any is complete and wrong, or complete where applicability decides, it is a soundness defect. Give the minimal reproduction and the fix location in csharp_demand.rs, likely where the positive rank-0 member match skips the base-list or inherited guard, but do not implement it. Same constraints as before.
I’ll make the local declaration control prove complete first, then run the four overload cases against the same temporary build and report the exact native responses.
The five-case fixture is compiling now. It includes a plain local method as a control, a source base, an unresolved base, two local overloads, and overloads split across partial files.

The test binary is still linking on the shared host. The control case will determine whether any incomplete overload result is meaningful evidence or just the same fixture-wide binding gap seen in the first pass.

The follow-up found three complete-answer soundness defects: an inapplicable derived method hid a valid source base target, an unresolved base still produced a complete answer, and local overloads produced complete ambiguity despite one applicable method. The partial-type case remained incomplete.

The [report](/workspace/28c4a33bde5b6bc0b4f4d45aa56e46bd/bifrost-dev/.mj/lanes/logs/c1-4e/complete-risk/REPORT.md) has the reproductions, native responses, and fix locations. The targeted test passed.

Parent (28c4a33b): decisive work, thank you. Please implement the fix; it is authorized. Brief: .mj/lanes/logs/c1-4e/APPLICABILITY-BRIEF.md. Worktree: .mj/lanes/7314-applicability, branch 7314-csharp-method-applicability-open, at origin/master ecb3b46353.
Ruling: until M6, a lookup whose selected targets include any method is never complete.
- Keep the targets: one method answers resolved-incomplete, several answer ambiguous-incomplete.
- Add one registered reason, csharp_method_applicability_unmodeled, classed Provider in read_ledger. Its evidence names the method group and any explicit base list.
- Apply it in one helper, used by both positive paths (rank-0 member and owner/qualified).
- Non-method members keep hiding.
- Add the golden: your four shapes with proven membership, plus a non-method control, hardwon.
- Add the epoch token -7314-csharp-method-applicability-open.
Hand back the items at the brief's end.
I’ll read the implementation brief, patch both positive lookup paths in the assigned worktree, add the golden coverage and epoch token, then run the required validation.

The lookup currently has no applicability check, and its positive paths bypass the inherited miss guard. I’ll attach the new provider gap when a selected declaration is a method, using one helper to read its kind and any explicit bases.

The implementation and golden case are in place. Formatting is taking longer than expected on the large source files; after it finishes, I’ll compile the focused golden to check that the provider gap reaches the public definition response.
The first build in this new worktree is compiling dependencies. The helper records the gap only for function declarations, so the field control should show whether non-method completion stays intact.

The implementation needs a design decision. The failing `M()` calls use Value lookup, while the agreed positive paths in `csharp_demand.rs` run only for Type lookup. The [report](/workspace/28c4a33bde5b6bc0b4f4d45aa56e46bd/bifrost-dev/.mj/lanes/logs/c1-4e/applicability/REPORT.md) documents three probes that left the complete answers unchanged. I asked the parent to choose a completion seam for Value answers. No commit or push was made.
I’ll trace the Value answer path and adapter lookup at the assigned master commit, then compare the registered language adapters. I’ll leave the worktree untouched and put the map in `MAP.md`.

The shared evaluator always has a positional fallback adapter, so “no language adapter” does not itself mean applicability is skipped. C# is different here: its parser marks the name as a CallableReference but publishes no call obligation, leaving the evaluator with no C# call row to refine. I’m mapping that boundary and the impact of a shared fallback rule.

The shared evaluator does consult applicability when a call obligation exists, even without a language adapter: it falls back to positional mapping. I’m checking the producer and answer projection now so the recommendation targets the missing call obligation precisely.
The read-only seam map is in [MAP.md](/workspace/28c4a33bde5b6bc0b4f4d45aa56e46bd/bifrost-dev/.mj/lanes/logs/c1-4e/applicability/MAP.md). The existing uncommitted worktree was left untouched.
